minimal_comment_summary: Keep the performance submission guard until the network reply finishes
root_cause: submit launches an unstructured Task and returns immediately, so the outer defer clears the guard while a performance request is still pending. The claim of a duplicate on the next tick overstates the timing: the monitor resets and needs another 12 seconds of observation.
evidence: Reviewed TVRequestsController.swift:171-190 starts the asynchronous request Task; :272-285 defers clearing submittingPerformance but calls submit synchronously.

Reviewed ShaderRequests.swift:199-218 resets a two-second warm-up and ten slow windows after emitting evidence. LocalTransport.swift uses a 30-second timeout, so a delayed response can outlast the observation interval.
ShaderRequestService.swift:285-288 deduplicates pending device/shader/source requests; this limits the issue to redundant capture/encoding/traffic rather than duplicate host work.
Current committed HEAD is d3b704dbae3284db04ff9d7f53be10abaebbe118; merged main 5ee08e1c78abfdf203fd2b256a15d14cd31338d0 has the same tree. Relevant uncommitted diffs do not remedy this finding.
regression_expectation: Delay request acknowledgement with a deterministic clock for longer than the observation interval. Assert one capture/submission until it resolves, preserve server deduplication, and use a bounded wall-clock backstop for any asynchronous test.

evidence: Reviewed shader_requests.py:380-388 converts every failing technical subprocess into CandidateError; :502-573 catches and sends it back into another implementation attempt.

The accepted product plan explicitly requires indefinite shader-defect repair and Mac cancellation of queued jobs only; preserve those rules while classifying unrecoverable baseline/configuration/runtime failures as operational.

minimal_comment_summary: Revoked parked or suspended repairing jobs never become terminal
root_cause: revoke marks repairing records revoked but does not terminalize them, while scheduling permanently excludes revoked records; execute also preserves suspended records for recovery without resolving this state.
evidence: Reviewed ShaderRequestService.swift:261-271 terminalizes queued and clarification/activation waits but omits non-active repairing jobs; :347-350 excludes revoked records.
The same file :440-442 moves a suspended active request to repairing; :423-438 skips terminal cleanup while suspended. verify/disable reject any non-terminal record at :225-246.
Existing tests cover queued revocation and interrupted repairing recovery separately, with no test of revocation during repairing.

regression_expectation: Assert terminal state and persisted unlock after revoking activation-repair, recovered, and suspended jobs, including revoke during process teardown.
